lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details that should be left off the résumé.
items.because: They are not needed to assess qualifications and can introduce irrelevant considerations into screening.

items.says: The eight-month gap between the B.A. and Operations Analyst role is unexplained.
items.because: It may leave readers uncertain whether the timeline is complete.

items.says: The 35% checkout-conversion result lacks a comparison basis and does not say whether the increase is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: Readers cannot judge the improvement’s size or reliability without the starting rate and comparison basis.

items.says: The dispute-self-service bullet gives a delivery result but no product or business outcome after launch.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what changed for users or the business.

items.says: The $1.1 million annual-loss claim overstates what six months of chargeback data establishes.
items.because: An annualized estimate requires a representative period and justified assumptions, and interviews do not validate a precise annual figure.

items.says: The roadmap outcome is described indirectly.
items.because: The long business-case phrase obscures what changed.

items.says: The open-ticket reduction lacks starting and ending counts and a precise comparison period.
items.because: Readers cannot judge its scale or distinguish a sustained reduction from a temporary change.

items.says: “Over the summer” is unnecessary time filler.
items.because: The entry already gives the internship dates.

items.says: The onboarding-measurement bullet gives a comparison method but no observed outcome.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether onboarding improved or what decision the measurement supported.

items.says: The strongest Harbor Payments achievement is not presented first.
The stated drop in late deliveries is wrong because excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the calculation, not necessarily delivery performance.
items.because: Removing late shipments can lower the reported rate without reducing the actual number or overall rate of late deliveries.

items.says: The delivery-rate comparison does not specify its period or shipments measured.
The 30% pick-error reduction does not say whether it is relative or in percentage points.
items.because: Those interpretations describe materially different operational gains.

items.says: “Cut warehouse pick errors 30%” omits “by.”
items.because: The wording is grammatically incomplete.

items.says: The strongest Crestline Logistics achievement is not presented first.
The S&OP bullet does not show the business effect of the work.
items.because: Readers cannot assess why the activity mattered.

items.says: The forecast-pack work lacks detail about the analysis behind it.
items.because: Readers cannot assess what substantive analyst skill it required.

items.says: “Prepares” uses present tense for an ended role.
items.because: It makes readers question whether the role is current.

items.says: The app-launch bullet does not identify the product decision, feature, or responsibility the candidate personally owned.
items.because: Readers cannot distinguish the candidate’s contribution from the venture’s overall achievement.

items.says: “With two dining halls” leaves the partnership relationship ambiguous.
items.because: It is unclear whether the app served students or was launched in partnership with the dining halls.

items.says: “Food that would have been thrown away” is passive and wordy.
items.because: It obscures the direct result.

items.says: The volunteer-system bullet does not clarify the two dining halls’ role.
items.because: It is unclear whether the system was implemented across the halls or created in collaboration with them.

items.says: The volunteer-system bullet uses inconsistent weekly phrasing.
The working-session bullet presents meetings instead of the scheduling analysis or improvement delivered.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what changed or what value the team lead created.

items.says: The working-session bullet gives no measure of the scheduling problem or result.
items.because: Without a before-and-after anchor, the practicum is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: The intake bullet uses passive, indirect wording.
items.because: It buries who mapped the process, shortened the form, and achieved the result.

items.says: The intake bullet does not show what the shortened form improved beyond adoption.
items.because: Adoption proves implementation rather than value, and four clinics measures scope rather than accomplishment.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result is wrong for the hospital practicum and duplicates a Harbor Payments achievement.
items.because: Merchants receiving payments do not fit the surrounding hospital work, making the résumé internally inconsistent.

items.says: If retained elsewhere, “it takes” should be in past tense.
If retained elsewhere, “across 2,300 merchants” should follow the result.
items.because: It currently interrupts the result.
